## Context limits

For the `document_url`/base64‑PDF endpoint used by Document QnA, the ceiling is whatever the chosen chat model's context window is — Document QnA is just OCR + a normal chat completion, not a separate service with its own window. Per the docs' limits table [1]:

| Model | Max context length |
|---|---|
| Mistral Large 3 | 256k |
| Mistral Medium 3.5 | 256k |
| Mistral Small 4 (`mistral-small-latest`) | 256k |
| Mistral Medium 3.1 | 128k |
| Codestral | 128k |

> "Requests exceeding the model's context window return a `400 Bad Request` error. Token counts include both input and output tokens." [1]

`mistral-small-latest` (the model shown in Mistral's own Document QnA examples) resolves to **Mistral Small 4, 256k tokens** [2]. Note that **321,774 prompt tokens is already above that 256k ceiling** — if that request actually returned a completion rather than a 400, you were on a model with a larger window (e.g. Large 3/Medium 3.5, also 256k, still exceeded — so check which model you actually called); otherwise this request should be right at/over the rejection boundary and worth double‑checking against the `400 Bad Request` behavior described above.

## Why a single-page PDF costs 321k tokens

Document QnA doesn't tokenize PDF text cheaply — it rasterizes each page to an image and tokenizes that image using the vision pipeline, at roughly:

> "≈ (ResolutionX * ResolutionY) / 784" for Mistral Small/Medium/Large-3-class models, capped at "1540x1540" max resolution ≈ **3025 tokens max per image** [3].

A normal PDF page therefore costs low thousands of tokens (Mistral's own example: a full page PDF via Document QnA used only 13,707 prompt tokens [4]). Getting to 321,774 tokens from *one page* means the page is effectively being split into many separate high-resolution image tiles/embedded images rather than one ~1540×1540 page render — typical causes:
- The "one page" PDF has a huge physical page size or embedded vector art at very high effective DPI, so Mistral's OCR/rendering step produces one giant image (or several tiled sub-images) instead of a single normal-resolution page.
- The PDF contains many embedded high-res images/figures on that one page, each tokenized separately under the same `(W×H)/784` formula (each image can cost up to ≈3025–4096 tokens depending on model [3], and multiple embedded images stack up fast).
- 308 kB file size itself isn't the driver — token cost tracks *rendered pixel resolution*, not file size, so a small file with one very large/high-DPI raster image inside is exactly the case that blows up token counts and 400-second latency.

**Fix:** downsample/flatten the PDF page to a reasonable resolution (well under 1540×1540 per rendered page/image) before sending it, or split out and downscale embedded images, to bring prompt tokens back down to the low-thousands range documented in Mistral's own example [4].

**Sources**
[1] https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/known-limitations#context-window
[2] https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-small-4-0-26-03
[3] https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/conversations/vision#how-many-tokens-correspond-to-an-image-andor-what-is-the-maximum-resolution
[4] https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/document-processing/document_qna#usage
